entry.content: Boudin painted skies that look gray until you try to mix them. This copy took a week, and the sky took five days of it.

entry.title: The wave: a woodblock study
entry.content: I cut five blocks to copy one wave. The blue block alone took a month, and I finally understand why the foam looks like fingers.
entry.summary: Cutting five blocks to understand one famous print.

entry.title: Keeping a commonplace book: sketchbook pages

link.title: Keeping a commonplace book: sketchbook pages

entry.content:
A commonplace book is a notebook of things worth keeping. Mine is a sketchbook with an index.1 Here is how it works.

The rules

  1. Write the date before anything else.
  2. Copy the source with every note, even a page number.
  3. Never delete an entry; cross it out instead.

Paper - a plain A5 book with numbered pages.

Index - the last four pages, by subject.

A worked example

Subject Pages Notes
Boats 4, 17, 52 pencil and wash
Hands 9, 10 from life
Skies 33 color notes

Draw what you see, not what you know.

When the notes moved to a computer I wrote a tiny script to rebuild the index:

boats   4 17 52
hands   9 10
skies   33

  1. The first one is from art school and mostly drawings of chairs. ↩
entry.summary: How I keep a sketchbook that I can still find things in, ten years later.

entry.title: Still life with a ledger
entry.content: The harbour office lent me its 1890 ledger for a week. I painted it open at the page where the tide tables begin.
entry.summary: Painting the old harbour accounts book, before it goes to the archive.
